stories.headline: Saeima approves €30M airBaltic loan after coalition reaches brink of collapse
stories.summary: Latvia's ruling coalition came close to breaking apart when coalition partner ZZS (Greens and Farmers) refused to back a €30 million state short-term loan to national airline airBaltic unless Transport Minister Atis Švinka (Progressives) resigned first. PM Siliņa publicly declared she was prepared to let the coalition fall rather than concede to the ultimatum; after days of crisis meetings, the coalition partners agreed to continue governing and the Saeima approved the loan. President Rinkēvičs, meeting separately with Siliņa, said airBaltic needs serious restructuring rather than ongoing state support. The episode unfolded against the backdrop of rising jet fuel prices and broader European airline distress.

stories.headline: Siliņa's Amsterdam airport VIP lounge use sparks political scandal; KNAB opens review
stories.summary: Former State Chancellery Director Jānis Citskovskis publicly accused PM Siliņa of unjustified use of the VIP lounge at Amsterdam Schiphol airport during a 2024 US visit, at a cost of roughly €4,184. Siliņa accused Citskovskis of defamation and threatened legal action, calling his statements a criminal defence tactic (Citskovskis himself faces a criminal case). KNAB announced it would review the allegations against both Siliņa and former PM Kariņš (whose daughter also used a VIP lounge at state expense, though costs were later deducted from his salary). President Rinkēvičs defended VIP lounge use by top officials on security grounds but declined to comment on Siliņa's specific case directly.

stories.headline: KNAB investigates New Unity ministers' expenses-paid trip to Lake Como seminar
stories.summary: PM Siliņa, several cabinet ministers, Riga city council representatives and Saeima faction members travelled to Italy for a three-day seminar on Moldovan elections, funded by the German Konrad Adenauer Foundation. KNAB announced it was examining whether the trip costs could constitute an impermissible gift from an NGO to a political party; no conclusions had been reached before the analysis date.

stories.headline: Baltic PM summit in Tallinn focuses on Rail Baltica, defence, and Hormuz navigation mission
stories.summary: The three Baltic prime ministers — Latvia's Siliņa, Estonia's Michal and Lithuania's Ruginienė — met in Tallinn on April 17 for the Baltic Council of Ministers, with Rail Baltica completion by 2030 as the centrepiece. Siliņa acknowledged Latvia's ongoing funding shortfalls and said heightened political attention to the project was not helpful. The meeting also addressed US arms delivery schedules (Latvia said its contracts were unchanged) and Latvia's potential contribution to a UK-France-led naval freedom-of-navigation mission in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Party ratings fall, public trust in coalition erodes ahead of October elections
stories.summary: Analysis of the latest Latvian party polling shows deepening public dissatisfaction, a large pool of undecided voters, and a broad sense that recent coalition scandals — Italy seminar, airBaltic, VIP lounge — have accumulated into a 'privilege aura' damaging New Unity. President Rinkēvičs separately observed that an unusually sharp pre-election battle for voters was already underway, with many voters disillusioned with their former choices.

stories.headline: President Rinkēvičs urges faster access to oncology and diabetes medicines
stories.summary: President Rinkēvičs met with patient activists and publicly called on the Health Ministry, government and Saeima to step-by-step address the availability of innovative medicines for cancer and diabetes patients. PM Siliņa told him that work was underway; Rinkēvičs said additional budget of around €150 million was being sought for 80 drugs.

stories.headline: Fiscal Discipline Council warns of serious budget deterioration without policy change
stories.summary: Latvia's Fiscal Discipline Council warned that, without active measures to raise revenues and cut spending, the country faces significant fiscal deterioration in the coming years. Debt servicing costs are projected to rise from 1.3% of GDP in 2026 to 1.6% by 2029–2030.

stories.headline: Sweden warns NATO that Russia may attempt to seize a Baltic Sea island as a provocation
stories.summary: Sweden's armed forces commander Mikael Klaesson warned in an interview with The Times that Russia could attempt to seize a Baltic Sea island in the near term to test NATO's reaction, and that a war conclusion in Ukraine would not mean peace in Europe — instead Russia would regroup and redirect resources westward. Latvian outlets picked up the warning.

stories.summary: Latvia's State Police announced plans to send preventive warning letters to 31 residents for using a platform designated as harmful on the internet. No further details about the platform were provided in available snippets.

stories.headline: NBS officers comment publicly on Belarus-Russia military cooperation in Ukraine war
stories.summary: Latvia's National Armed Forces officers — including Major Jānis Slaidiņš — gave public commentary on Russian military developments: Belarus is increasingly involved in supporting Russia's war effort, and Russia is using cover of medical facilities for weapons manufacturing at 48 identified plants.

stories.headline: Rinkēvičs demands two-week deadline to resolve electronic voter register questions ahead of October elections
stories.summary: President Rinkēvičs set a deadline of early May for authorities to clarify the functioning of Latvia's online voter registration system and to have a clear alternative plan ready if concerns arise, ahead of the October 3 Saeima elections. He stressed that election legitimacy is the main priority.

stories.headline: French Rafale jets display NATO presence at Latvia's Lielvārde airbase
stories.summary: Two French Rafale fighter jets, currently stationed in Lithuania as part of NATO air policing, visited Latvia's Lielvārde airbase on April 14. PM Siliņa, Defence Minister Sprūds and Foreign Affairs Minister Braže attended the display event alongside the French ambassador.

stories.headline: Saeima adopts anti-SLAPP amendments protecting journalists from abusive litigation
stories.summary: Latvia's Saeima passed third-reading amendments to the law on protection of persons involved in public interest activities and related Civil Procedure Law changes, implementing the EU anti-SLAPP directive (transposition deadline: May 7, 2026). The Justice Ministry framed the changes as protection for free speech and public debate.
